questions.question: A shopkeeper buys a product for Rs.80 and marks a price assuming a profit of 50% on his cost price. At the time of making the sale, he gives a 20% discount on the marked price. What is the amount of net profit he makes on this product?

Markup% = 50% (As he marks a price assuming a profit of 50% on CP)

So, Marked Price = Rs.80 + 50% of Rs.80

 = Rs.80 + Rs.40 

 = Rs.120

Discount% = 20% 

So, Selling Price = Marked Price - Discount

 = Rs.120 - 20% of Rs.120

 = Rs.120 - Rs.24

 = Rs.96

Net Profit = SP - CP

 = Rs.96 - Rs.80

 = Rs.16

Hence, **Net Profit = Rs.16**

questions.question: When a large force acts on a body for a short time, then the force is called?
questions.solution:
__
 
• When a large force acts on a body for a short time, then the force is called **impulsive force.__**
 
• Impulse = force x time = change in momentum
 
• Impulse is a vector quantity.
 
• SI Unit of Impulse is Newton second (Ns).

__**Explanation:**__

Impulse

 
• When a large force works on a body for a very small time interval, it is called impulsive force.
 
• An impulsive force does not remain constant, but changes first from zero to maximum and then from maximum to zero. In such a case, we measure the total effect of force.
 
• The impulse caused by a force during a specific time interval is equal to the body's change of momentum during that time interval.
 
• Impulse, effectively, is a measure of change in momentum.
 
• The impulse of a force is a measure of the total effect of force.
 
• Impulse is a vector quantity and its direction is the same as that of force.
 
• SI unit of impulse is Newton-second or kg-m-s-1 and CGS unit is g.m/s

Select the correct answer from the codes given below:

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__option 2.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Muslim League**

 
 
• It was founded in 1906 as an alternative political group to the Indian National Congress.
 
• Muhammad Ali Jinnah was elected as president in 1916.
 
• Following the First World War (1914-18) the Muslim League joined forces with Congress to advocate for Home Rule within the British Empire.
 
• The founders of the Muslim League were: Khwaja Salimullah, Vikar-ul-Mulk, Syed Amir Ali, Syed Nabiullah, Khan Bahadur Ghulam and Mustafa Chowdhury.
 
 
 
• **Cabinet Mission Plan**
 
 
• It was a high-powered mission sent in February 1946 to India by the Atlee Government (then British Prime Minister).
 
• The mission had three British cabinet members – Pethick Lawrence, Stafford Cripps, & and A.V. Alexander.
 
• The aim was to discuss the transfer of power from British to Indian leadership.
 
 
 
• In 1946, elections to the Constituent Assembly were held following the proposals of the British Cabinet Mission.
 
• In this election, the Congress obtained a majority in the Assembly, and the Muslim League consolidated its support among the Muslim electorate.
 
• **The Muslim league first approved the plan. But when the Muslim League found out that Congress had the majority in the Constituent Assembly, they rejected the plan**. **Hence A is true.**
 
• On 29 July 1946, the Muslim League withdrew its acceptance of the Mission Plan and declared Direct Action.
 
• The Muslim League joined the interim government formed in 1946 on 26 October 1946. **Hence R is true**.
 
• Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.question: _________ is an assessment of economic production in an economy that includes current prices in its calculation.
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Nominal GDP is an assessment of economic production in an economy but includes the current prices of goods and services in its calculation**__.

 __
 
• Nominal GDP measures a country's gross domestic product** using current prices,** without adjusting for inflation. 
 
• Contrast this with real GDP, which measures a country's economic output adjusted for the impact of inflation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Real GDP** - The sum of all goods and services produced at **constant prices.**

 
 
• The prices used in determining GDP are based on a certain base year or previous year. 
 
• It provides a more accurate account of economic growth, as it is already an inflation-adjusted measure, meaning that the effects of inflation are excluded.
 
 
 
• **Actual GDP** - A real-time measure of all output at any given interval or at any point in time.
 
 
• It displays the current state of business of the economy.
 
 
 
• **Potential GDP** - Ideal economic conditions with 100% employment in all sectors, stable currency, and stable product prices.

questions.question: Which of the following measures the magnitude of an earthquake?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Richter scale**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Richter scale** is a logarithmic scale used to measure the **magnitude of earthquakes**.
 
• It was developed in **1935** by **Charles F. Richter**, a seismologist, in collaboration with Beno Gutenberg.
 
• The scale quantifies the **amount of energy released** during an earthquake.
 
• It is based on measurements of the amplitude of seismic waves recorded by a **seismograph**.
 
• The scale is logarithmic, meaning each whole number increase represents a **tenfold increase in amplitude** and approximately 31.6 times more energy release.
 
• The Richter scale is suitable for measuring the magnitude of small to medium earthquakes but is not as effective for very large earthquakes.
 
• This scale is essential for seismologists to assess the intensity of an earthquake and its potential impact.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Explanation of Other Options:**

 
 
• **Polygraph:** Also known as a lie detector, it measures physiological responses such as **heart rate, blood pressure, and respiration** to assess truthfulness. It is not related to earthquake measurement.
 
• **Barometer:** This instrument is used to measure **atmospheric pressure**. It is commonly used in weather forecasting but has no connection to earthquake magnitude.
 
• **Thermometer:** A thermometer measures **temperature**, whether it is of the environment, human body, or any other system. It is irrelevant to seismology.
 
 
 
• **Richter Scale Characteristics:**
 
 
• The scale ranges from **1 to 10**, where values below 2 are typically not felt by humans, and values above 7 represent major earthquakes with potential for significant destruction.
 
• The largest earthquake ever recorded on the Richter scale was the **1960 Valdivia earthquake** in Chile, with a magnitude of 9.5.
 
 
 
• **Modern Advances:**
 
 
• While the Richter scale is historically significant, modern seismologists use the **Moment Magnitude Scale (Mw)**, which provides more accurate measurements of large earthquakes.
 
• Both scales are logarithmic and are consistent for small to medium earthquakes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Seismographs:**

 
 
• These instruments are used to record **seismic waves** generated by earthquakes.
 
• Seismographs detect ground motion and create a visual representation called a **seismogram**.
 
 
 
• **Earthquake Preparedness:**
 
 
• Knowing the magnitude and location of an earthquake helps in **disaster management** and preparedness.
 
• Countries like **Japan** and the **United States** have advanced seismic monitoring systems to mitigate earthquake-related risks.

questions.question: Who among the following is known as the Father of the Communal Electorate in India?

__
 
• Lord Minto, who served as the Viceroy of India from 1905 to 1910, is regarded as the "Father of the Communal Electorate" in India.
 
• The concept of communal electorates was introduced in the Indian Councils Act of 1909, also known as the Morley-Minto Reforms.
 
• This reform allowed separate electorates for Muslims, where only Muslims could vote for Muslim candidates in designated constituencies.
 
• The idea aimed to address the political representation of Muslims in India but eventually led to the politicization of religious identities.
 
• The introduction of communal electorates sowed the seeds of division between Hindus and Muslims, which later became a significant factor in India's partition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Morley:**

 
 
• Lord Morley was the Secretary of State for India during the Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909.
 
• He played a significant role in drafting the reforms, which introduced limited constitutional changes, including the communal electorates.
 
• Although he worked closely with Lord Minto, Morley's role was more administrative and policy-focused rather than direct involvement in India.
 
 
 
• **Lord Chelmsford:**
 
 
• Lord Chelmsford served as the Viceroy of India from 1916 to 1921.
 
• He is best known for the Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms of 1919, which introduced the system of dyarchy in provincial governance.
 
• These reforms expanded the scope of Indian representation but did not introduce communal electorates.
 
 
 
• **Lord Metcalfe:**
 
 
• Lord Metcalfe was the acting Governor-General of India from 1835 to 1836.
 
• He is remembered for his efforts to promote press freedom in India by repealing restrictions on the press.
 
• His contributions are unrelated to the concept of communal electorates or constitutional reforms.

questions.question: The magnificent temple at Gangaikonda Cholapuram was commissioned by which Chola ruler?

The correct answer is __**Rajendra Chola I**__.

__
 
• The **magnificent temple at Gangaikonda Cholapuram** was commissioned by **Rajendra Chola I**, a ruler of the Chola dynasty in South India.
 
• **Rajendra Chola I** was the son and successor of **Rajaraja Chola I**, who was also a great temple builder.
 
• The temple was built to commemorate Rajendra Chola I's **victories in Northern India**, particularly his successful campaign to bring the waters of the Ganges to his kingdom.
 
• Gangaikonda Cholapuram was established as the **capital of the Chola empire** during the reign of Rajendra Chola I, replacing Thanjavur.
 
• The temple is an architectural marvel and is part of the group of **Great Living Chola Temples**, which are recognized as a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.
 
• The temple is known for its **massive vimana** (tower) and intricate carvings that reflect the artistic and cultural brilliance of the Chola dynasty.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rajendra Chola I:**

 
 
• Rajendra Chola I ruled from **1014 CE to 1044 CE** and is considered one of the greatest rulers of the Chola dynasty.
 
• He expanded the Chola empire to its greatest extent, covering parts of present-day **India, Sri Lanka, Maldives, Malaysia, and Indonesia**.
 
• Rajendra Chola I is also credited with establishing a strong naval force, enabling the Cholas to dominate maritime trade and politics in the Indian Ocean region.
 
 
 
• **Gangaikonda Cholapuram Temple:**
 
 
• The temple is an example of **Dravidian architecture**, featuring exquisite sculptures and carvings.
 
• The temple's **vimana** (tower) is slightly shorter than the Brihadeshwara Temple in Thanjavur but is more intricately designed.
 
• The temple was dedicated to **Lord Shiva** and houses a massive Shiva Lingam in its sanctum.
 
• The bronze sculptures and stone carvings in the temple depict scenes from Hindu mythology and reflect the artistic advancements of the Chola period.
 
 
 
• **Great Living Chola Temples:**
 
 
• The group includes three temples: **Brihadeshwara Temple at Thanjavur**, **Gangaikonda Cholapuram Temple**, and **Airavatesvara Temple at Darasuram**.
 
• These temples were recognized as a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** in 1987 due to their architectural and cultural significance.
 
 
 
• **Other Rulers of the Chola Dynasty:**
 
 
• **Rajaraja Chola I:** Known for building the Brihadeshwara Temple in Thanjavur.
 
• **Rajadhiraja Chola I:** Successor of Rajendra Chola I, who continued the military campaigns and architectural endeavors of the Chola dynasty.
 
• **Kulothunga Chola I:** Known for consolidating the Chola empire and fostering trade relations with Southeast Asia.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The Chola dynasty is renowned for its contributions to **art, architecture, and administration**.
 
• Their temple architecture, especially the use of granite and intricate carvings, set a benchmark in South Indian architecture.
 
• The Chola kings were great patrons of **Shaivism**, and their temples often featured grand Shiva Lingams and elaborately designed sanctums.
 
• The Chola dynasty also excelled in maritime trade, with ports such as Nagapattinam and Poompuhar serving as key trade hubs.

questions.question: The hoisting of a 'Gudi' flag, symbolizing the victory of good over evil, is a prominent ritual in which festival celebrated in Maharashtra?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gudi Padwa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Gudi Padwa** is a springtime festival that marks the traditional New Year for Maharashtrians and Konkani Hindus.
 
• Celebrated on the first day of the Hindu lunisolar calendar month of **Chaitra**, it typically falls in March or April.
 
• The festival is marked by the hoisting of a **'Gudi'**, a flag made using a bamboo pole covered with a bright cloth and adorned with neem leaves, mango leaves, and a garland of flowers, symbolizing **victory and prosperity**.
 
• It celebrates the mythical victory of **Lord Rama** over Ravana and the return of Rama to Ayodhya, signifying the triumph of good over evil.
 
• Gudi Padwa also heralds the arrival of spring and the harvest season, making it an agrarian festival in Maharashtra.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Navratri**

 
 
• Navratri is a nine-day Hindu festival dedicated to the worship of Goddess Durga and her nine forms.
 
• It is celebrated twice a year – once during spring (Chaitra Navratri) and once during autumn (Sharad Navratri).
 
• Each day is associated with a specific manifestation of Durga, including Kali, Saraswati, and Lakshmi.
 
• The festival is marked by fasting, pujas, and cultural performances, such as Garba and Dandiya dances.
 
 
 
• **Janmashtami**
 
 
• Janmashtami celebrates the birth of **Lord Krishna**, the eighth avatar of Vishnu.
 
• It is observed on the eighth day of Krishna Paksha (dark fortnight) of the month of **Bhadrapada** in the Hindu calendar.
 
• The festival involves night-long celebrations, including bhajans, dances, and reenactments of Krishna's life, particularly his childhood.
 
• The ritual of **Dahi Handi**, where pots of curd are broken by teams of participants, is a popular event during Janmashtami.
 
 
 
• **Durga Puja**
 
 
• Durga Puja is a major Hindu festival, especially celebrated in West Bengal and other eastern states of India.
 
• It honors Goddess Durga's victory over the demon Mahishasura, symbolizing the triumph of good over evil.
 
• The festival spans ten days, culminating in Vijayadashami, when idols of Durga are immersed in water bodies.
 
• It is known for grand pandals, artistic decorations, cultural performances, and traditional feasts.
 
 
 
• **Theme of the Question**
 
 
• The question pertains to festivals celebrated in India, with an emphasis on their symbolic and cultural significance.
 
• Festivals like Gudi Padwa, Navratri, Janmashtami, and Durga Puja represent India's rich cultural diversity, spirituality, and agrarian roots.
 
• Such celebrations often involve rituals, prayers, and community gatherings to spread joy and positivity among people.

questions.question: If 49 litres of a milk solution has 63% milk in it, then how much milk should be added to make the concentration of milk 70% in the solution?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Equating the constant quantity of water before and after adding milk:

Initial Water % × Initial Volume = Final Water % × Final Volume

⇒ 37% × 49 = 30% × Final Volume

⇒ Final Volume = (37 × 49) ÷ 30 = 1813 ÷ 30 L

⇒ Added Milk = Final Volume − Initial Volume = (1813 ÷ 30) − 49 = 343 ÷ 30 = 11 ¹³/₃₀ litres

**∴ The correct answer is 11 ¹³/₃₀ litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total volume of initial mixture = 49 litres

Milk concentration in initial mixture = 63%

Desired milk concentration in final mixture = 70%

Concentration of pure milk added = 100%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/49b68d247ebe9a0f2e81a11e747f873037ac07891b24a6e0135a4d85f3d00d7a.png] 

**Calculations:**

Using the rule of alligation, the ratio in which the initial mixture and pure milk must be mixed is:

⇒ Ratio = (100 − 70) : (70 − 63)

⇒ Ratio = 30 : 7

We are given that 30 units of the initial mixture corresponds to 49 litres.

⇒ 30 units = 49 L

⇒ 1 unit = 49 ÷ 30 L

⇒ Pure milk to be added (7 units) = 7 × (49 ÷ 30) = 343 ÷ 30 L

⇒ Quantity of milk added = 11 ¹³/₃₀ litres

**∴ The correct answer is 11 ¹³/₃₀ litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rule of Alligation

It is a visual mathematical method used to find the ratio in which two ingredients at their respective concentrations must be mixed to produce a mixture of a desired average concentration. The ratio is determined by cross-subtracting the target value from the components.

Constant Quantity Method

When only one component (e.g., milk) is added or removed from a mixture, the absolute quantity of the other component (e.g., water) remains strictly unchanged. Equating the initial and final volumes of this unchanged part yields the new total volume directly.

Replacement Formula

When a specific volume of a mixture is repeatedly replaced by one of its pure components, the remaining amount of the original un-added component is calculated as: Final Amount = Initial Amount × (1 − Replaced Volume ÷ Total Volume)ⁿ.
</p

questions.question: A number is increased by 30% and then again increased by 30%. By what percentage should the increased number be reduced so as to get back the original number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Two successive increases of 30% result in a net increase of 30 + 30 + (30 × 30) / 100 = 69%.

Let the original number be 100, which means the final increased number becomes 169.

To restore the original number, we must reduce 169 by 69.

Required percentage reduction = (69 / 169) × 100 = 40.82%.

**∴ The correct answer is 40.82%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ First increase = 30%

⇒ Second increase = 30%

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Effective percentage increase = x + y + (x × y) / 100

⇒ Percentage reduction = (Decrease in value / Increased value) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9b90c1a6e26ea04f740c04920aab4423856d54f34484298801e3c5e57e4211f3.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Effective increase = 30 + 30 + (30 × 30) / 100 = 69%

⇒ Let the original number be 100.

⇒ The increased number = 100 + 69 = 169.

⇒ To get back to the original number, required reduction = 169 − 100 = 69.

⇒ Required percentage reduction = (69 / 169) × 100

⇒ Required percentage reduction = 6900 / 169 ≈ 40.82%

**∴ The correct answer is 40.82%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value experiences two successive percentage changes of a% and b%, the effective overall change is calculated using the formula: Net Change = a + b + (a × b) / 100. This is useful for sequential profit, discounts, or population changes.

Reversal of Percentage Change

If a quantity is increased by x%, restoring it to its original value requires a percentage reduction of (x ÷ (100 + x)) × 100%. In this case, with a 69% overall increase, the required reduction is (69 ÷ 169) × 100%.

Base Value Concept in Percentages

Percentages are strictly relative to a defined base value. Moving from 100 to 169 uses 100 as the base (69% increase). Reversing from 169 to 100 uses 169 as the new base, resulting in a significantly lower percentage figure despite identical absolute changes.
</p

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 1500 amounts to Rs. 2175 in 3 years at simple interest. If rate of interest is increased by 3 percent, then what will be the new amount?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Extra interest generated by the 3% rate increase over 3 years = (P × Extra Rate × T) ÷ 100

⇒ Extra SI = (1500 × 3 × 3) ÷ 100 = Rs. 135

New Amount = Initial Amount + Extra SI

⇒ New Amount = 2175 + 135 = 2310

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2310.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = Rs. 1500

Amount in 3 years (A) = Rs. 2175

Time (T) = 3 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

Amount = Principal + SI

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0c659e1767799b38ff4968967fc52c5da8296c39a13182a83a5d33da3159b767.png] 

**Calculation:**

⇒ SI = A − P

⇒ SI = 2175 − 1500 = Rs. 675

⇒ 675 = (1500 × R × 3) ÷ 100

⇒ 675 = 45 × R

⇒ R = 675 ÷ 45 = 15%

Now, the new rate of interest = 15% + 3% = 18%

⇒ New SI = (1500 × 18 × 3) ÷ 100

⇒ New SI = 45 × 18 = Rs. 810

⇒ New Amount = P + New SI

⇒ New Amount = 1500 + 810 = Rs. 2310

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 2310.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest

When interest is compounded annually, the amount is calculated as: Amount = P × (1 + R ÷ 100)T.

SI vs CI Difference

The difference between Compound Interest and Simple Interest for 2 years on the same principal is calculated as: Difference = P × (R ÷ 100)².

Rule of 72

A quick mental math shortcut to estimate the number of years required to double your money at a given annual interest rate. Time to double ≈ 72 ÷ Rate of Interest.
</p

questions.question: A businessman marks his goods 20% more than their cost price. By giving a certain discount he suffers a loss of 4%. What percentage discount did he give?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the Cost Price (CP) of the goods be 100.

Marked Price (MP) = 100 + 20% of 100 = 120.

Selling Price (SP) = 100 − 4% of 100 = 96.

Discount = MP − SP = 120 − 96 = 24.

Discount Percentage = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100 = (24 ÷ 120) × 100 = 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Markup Percentage = 20%

Loss Percentage = 4%

MP ÷ CP = (100 − Loss %) ÷ (100 − Discount %)

**Calculation:**

Let CP be 100.

⇒ MP = 100 × (120 ÷ 100) = 120

⇒ 120 ÷ 100 = (100 − 4) ÷ (100 − Discount %)

⇒ 1.2 = 96 ÷ (100 − Discount %)

⇒ 100 − Discount % = 96 ÷ 1.2

⇒ 100 − Discount % = 80

⇒ Discount % = 100 − 80 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP) and Cost Price (CP) Relation

The ratio of Marked Price to Cost Price can be directly calculated using the formula: MP ÷ CP = (100 ± Profit/Loss %) ÷ (100 − Discount %).

Successive Discounts

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given, the equivalent single discount is given by: (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

Dishonest Dealer Concept

When a dealer claims to sell at the cost price but uses a false weight, the actual Profit % is calculated as: (True Weight − False Weight) ÷ False Weight × 100.
</p

By cross-multiplying the given equation:

⇒ tanθ + cotθ = 2 × (tanθ − cotθ)

⇒ tanθ + cotθ = 2tanθ − 2cotθ

Bringing similar terms to one side:

⇒ 2cotθ + cotθ = 2tanθ − tanθ

⇒ 3cotθ = tanθ

We know that cotθ = 1 / tanθ, substituting this back into the equation:

⇒ 3 × (1 / tanθ) = tanθ

questions.question: A select group of 4 is to be formed from 8 men and 6 women in such a way that the group must have at least 1 woman. In how many different ways can it be done?

Total ways with at least 1 woman = (Total ways to choose 4 people) − (Ways to choose 4 men only)

⇒ ⁸C₄ = (8 × 7 × 6 × 5) ÷ (4 × 3 × 2 × 1) = 70

⇒ Required ways = 1001 − 70 = 931

**∴ The correct answer is 931 ways.**

Number of women = 6

Total people = 14

ⁿCᵣ = n! ÷ [r! × (n − r)!]

⇒ Total different ways = 336 + 420 + 160 + 15 = 931

Permutations (Arrangements)

"At Least" Concept

To calculate "at least 1", it is generally faster to use the rule: Total combinations − Combinations with 0 occurrences.

questions.question: If the number 678967# is exactly divisible by 72, the minimum value of # is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

72 = 8 × 9, so the number must be divisible by both 8 and 9.

For divisibility by 8, check the last 3 digits: 67#.

67# ÷ 8 leaves a remainder of 3#, and 32 is the only multiple of 8 in the 30s, so # = 2.

Checking divisibility by 9: Sum of digits = 6 + 7 + 8 + 9 + 6 + 7 + 2 = 45, which is exactly divisible by 9.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number = 678967#

Divisor = 72

**Formula Used:**

A number is divisible by 72 if it is exactly divisible by both 8 and 9 (which are co-prime factors of 72).

**Calculations:**

⇒ Divisibility by 8: The number formed by the last three digits (67#) must be exactly divisible by 8.

⇒ 67# = 670 + #

⇒ 670 ÷ 8 = 83 with a remainder of 6.

⇒ So, 6 + # must be exactly divisible by 8.

⇒ Since # is a single digit from 0 to 9, the only possible value is # = 2 (as 6 + 2 = 8).

⇒ Divisibility by 9: The sum of all the digits must be exactly divisible by 9.

⇒ Sum of digits = 6 + 7 + 8 + 9 + 6 + 7 + #

⇒ Sum = 43 + #

⇒ Substituting # = 2, we get: Sum = 43 + 2 = 45.

⇒ 45 is perfectly divisible by 9, meaning both conditions are fully satisfied.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 8

A number is exactly divisible by 8 if the number formed by its last three digits is a multiple of 8.

Divisibility Rule of 9

A number is exactly divisible by 9 if the sum of all its individual digits is a multiple of 9.

Co-prime Factorization

To check divisibility by a composite number (like 72), break it down into co-prime factors (8 and 9) and test divisibility for each factor individually.

Divisibility Rule of 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of digits at odd places and the sum of digits at even places is either 0 or a multiple of 11.
</p

⇒ 2x = 110°

⇒ x = 55°

⇒ Therefore, ∠N = 55°

questions.question: The price of two types of rice is Rs. 15/kg and Rs. 20/kg. If both the types are mixed in the ratio 3 ∶ 2 respectively, then what is the price per kg of the mixed variety of rice?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the weighted average method for direct calculation of the mixed price:

Mean Price = (Price₁ × Quantity₁ + Price₂ × Quantity₂) ÷ (Quantity₁ + Quantity₂)

Mean Price = (15 × 3 + 20 × 2) ÷ (3 + 2)

Mean Price = (45 + 40) ÷ 5

Mean Price = 85 ÷ 5 = 17

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 17.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Price of Type 1 rice = Rs. 15/kg

Price of Type 2 rice = Rs. 20/kg

Mixing ratio = 3 : 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4dee0c8f93fe1b472c56c7a00e5b7aac926a7460086c017d95290428fc395421.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Rule of Alligation: (Quantity of Cheaper) ÷ (Quantity of Dearer) = (Price of Dearer − Mean Price) ÷ (Mean Price − Price of Cheaper)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the mean price of the mixture be x.

⇒ From the rule of alligation, the ratio of quantities is given by the cross differences.

⇒ (20 − x) ÷ (x − 15) = 3 ÷ 2

⇒ 2 × (20 − x) = 3 × (x − 15)

⇒ 40 − 2x = 3x − 45

⇒ 2x + 3x = 40 + 45

⇒ 5x = 85

⇒ x = 17

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 17.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rule of Alligation

It establishes the relationship between prices and quantities of two ingredients mixed together: (Quantity of Cheaper) ÷ (Quantity of Dearer) = (Price of Dearer − Mean Price) ÷ (Mean Price − Price of Cheaper).

Weighted Average

When multiple components have different weights or ratios, their combined average can be evaluated systematically using the formula Aw = (w₁x₁ + w₂x₂) ÷ (w₁ + w₂).

Replacement Formula

If V is the total volume of a liquid, and x volume is drawn out and replaced with an identical volume of water repeated n times, the final quantity of pure liquid remaining is: V × (1 − x ÷ V)ⁿ.

questions.question: A thief is spotted by a policeman from a distance of 400 metres. When the policeman starts to chase the thief also starts running. If the speed of the thief is18 km/h and that of the policeman 20 km/h, then how far would the thief have run before he is overtaken?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of speeds (Thief : Policeman) = 18 : 20 = 9 : 10

Since time is constant, the ratio of distances covered = 9 : 10

Difference in ratio parts = 10 − 9 = 1 part

1 part represents the initial gap = 400 m

Distance run by the thief = 9 parts = 9 × 400 m = 3600 m = 3.6 km

**∴ The correct answer is 3.6 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial distance between them = 400 m = 0.4 km

Speed of thief = 18 km/h

Speed of policeman = 20 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed = Speed of Policeman − Speed of Thief

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/97d6e706c6a3abad4bfd017325bc11c9ad98957a78969de0b5524dbc4ae4ed39.png] 

⇒ Relative speed = 20 − 18 = 2 km/h

⇒ Time taken to overtake = 0.4 km ÷ 2 km/h = 0.2 hours

⇒ Distance run by the thief = Speed of thief × Time taken

⇒ Distance run by the thief = 18 km/h × 0.2 hours = 3.6 km

**∴ The correct answer is 3.6 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their individual speeds (S₁ − S₂).

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two bodies move towards each other in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Constant Time Concept

If the time of travel is the same for two moving objects, the ratio of the distance covered by them is exactly equal to the ratio of their respective speeds (D₁ : D₂ = S₁ : S₂).
</p
